prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Make an original Brazilian literary book cover, complete flat 1024x1536 portrait. Text exactly "IRACEMA" and "JOSÉ DE ALENCAR". Bold art direction: 1920s Brazilian modernist gouache, broad flat organic forms, tender terracotta, saturated forest green, dusty pink and warm yellow, few confident handmade brush marks. A thoughtful Indigenous Brazilian woman seen in dignified profile, long flowing black hair visually becoming a coastline and a green leaf; no exoticized nudity, no feather headdress, no fantasy armor. Expressive composition with strong asymmetrical cropping and abstract flora; not a photographic scene and not a landscape postcard. Title IRACEMA in large hand-painted rounded uppercase, arranged in a dynamic vertical block on the right half without obscuring the face; author small but legible aligned left at lower edge. Rich ink on matte paper. All lettering accurate and clear at thumbnail scale, no publisher logo, no extra text, no border. Distinctive literary illustration with mature editorial sensibility.

Use case: illustration-story. Create a complete original front cover 1024x1536 portrait for Brazilian novel "O CORTIÇO" by "ALUÍSIO AZEVEDO". Art direction: typographic architecture, almost ALL TYPE, distressed wood-type letterpress urban modernism. Off-white massive slab-serif letters stacked O / COR / TIÇO become rows of densely packed tenement windows, incorporate a few tiny black rectangles within letters like windows and three thin diagonal clotheslines. Burnt sienna and charcoal background blocks, electric yellow small accent, a tactile printed texture. No people illustration, no picturesque landscape, no sunset. Large lettering occupies nearly entire cover with asymmetrical building-like rhythm, exceptionally legible. Author vertically down left margin in yellow narrow sans serif, not at the bottom. Title must read O CORTIÇO with Ç clearly correct; author ALUÍSIO AZEVEDO accent correct. No extra words, no fake publisher, no border, no mockup. Striking thoughtful graphic design that connects typographic density to collective urban life.
